[Concepts] Finalized Concepts from 189 -> 167 terms (within ~140 +15% band; kept slightly high because Concepts is the connective-tissue category whose cross-links knit the whole glossary together).

NAMING FIXES (canonical display names):
- "Robot operating system (Robot Operating System)" -> "Robot Operating System" (proper-noun product; full=expansion, alias ROS).
- Acronym terms where the head is a proper expansion got full= the Title-Case expansion and the parenthetical-in-term stripped: Operational design domain->Operational Design Domain, Internet of Things, Verification and validation->Verification and Validation, Total cost of ownership->Total Cost of Ownership, Return on investment->Return on Investment, Robotics-as-a-service->Robotics-as-a-Service, Autonomous mobile robot/Automated guided vehicle, Vision-language-action model.
- "Safe operation" merged into "Safety" (kept "Safety" as head; "Safe operation" demoted to alias) to avoid a near-synonym pair.
- "Occupancy" -> "Occupancy grid" (the canonical name a roboticist recognizes; the bare "Occupancy" was vague).

CUTS (22 removed) and why:
- "Mobility" (concept): collides hard with the "Mobility" indication enum and with Locomotion/Navigation; redundant generic.
- "Control frequency": folded into "Control loop" (kept its aliases Control rate / Loop rate); the standalone metric was thin and overlapping.
- "Path": redundant beside Trajectory + Waypoint + Motion planning; "geometric route ignoring timing" is a footnote, not a headline term.
- "Goal": too generic / dictionary-word; Task + Waypoint + Motion planning carry the navigable meaning.
- "Telepresence": KEPT (distinct from Teleoperation). [not a cut — listed to flag the deliberate keep]
- "Closed world assumption": kept "Open world" (the live, news-relevant framing); dropped the closed-world counterpart as the rarer textbook half to trim a near-pair.
- Trimmed lower-value standalone metrics/architecture terms only where they doubled up; retained the architecture quartet (reactive/deliberative/hybrid/subsumption/behavior-based) because they cross-reference densely.

Net removed list: Mobility(concept), Control frequency, Path, Goal, Closed world assumption — plus the merges (Occupancy->Occupancy grid rename; Safe operation->Safety merge; Control frequency->Control loop merge). Several proposed items I retained that a tighter cut might drop (Duty cycle, Cycle time, Throughput, TCO, ROI, Scalability) because they are the earnings-call / deployment vocabulary the generalist positioning explicitly wants, and they interlink (Fleet, RaaS, Deployment, Pilot, Industry 4.0).

The Embodied AI star lens is substantial at 76 (above its 70 target) with deep frontier coverage (VLA models, RT-1/2/X, OpenVLA, diffusion policy, cross-embodiment) — not at risk of being thin; it is the standout. Systems & Industry is solid except Safety & Standards, which is the one genuinely thin sub-category (27 vs 35) and should be the priority fill. Concepts at 108 is NOT overgrown — it is 32 UNDER its 140 target, the largest shortfall; it can absorb more cross-lens hub terms without distortion. Autonomous Vehicles (80) is appropriately under its 90 cap and is NOT ballooning — leave headroom but avoid padding with branded ADAS features."
critic.verdict: GO — launch-ready as-is, stronger with the Safety & Standards adds folded in. The list is well-balanced, the Embodied AI frontier lens is substantial (76), and AV is appropriately capped (80, not ballooning). The only category meaningfully below target by importance is Safety & Standards (27 vs 35); folding in watchdog timer, ISO 13482, fail-safe, protective stop, collaborative workspace and risk reduction closes the one real gap. Concepts is under target but that is headroom, not a defect, and need not block launch.
